{
  "ceo_summary": "Implementing this lightweight server significantly expands our smoke testing surface area, guaranteeing robust connectivity validation across all deployment environments.",
  "constraints": [
    "Must implement a minimal HTTP server capable of echoing received requests (GET/POST).",
    "Must use a structured logging format (e.g., JSON) for all access, error, and lifecycle events.",
    "Should expose a clear API/interface for programmatic invocation by the CI test runner.",
    "Must be dependency-managed and kept isolated from core business logic."
  ],
  "cpo_summary": "We must ensure the library adheres to clean architecture principles, keeping the server implementation highly modular and the logging mechanism standardized for easy integration with existing monitoring tools.",
  "modality": "library",
  "rationale": "The HTTP echo server is a reusable utility component that provides core functionality for the smoke testing suite. Structuring it as a library ensures it can be easily integrated as a dependency within the existing CI framework without polluting the main application codebase."
}

  "primary_language": "C++",
  "required_dependencies": [
    "Boost.Asio (or equivalent networking library)",
    "nlohmann/json (or similar JSON library)"
  ],
  "testing_strategy": "Unit tests for request handlers and serialization logic; Integration tests simulating full HTTP request/response cycles."
}
